Definition: of Latin origin; Cæsar, a title of the Roman emperor:--Cæsar.
BiblicalUsage: Kaisar is Caesar, the title of the Roman emperor, and the name that stood behind every tax, every census, and every appeal in the New Testament. The Pharisees ask whether it is lawful to give tribute unto Caesar; Jesus answers, render unto Caesar the things that are Caesar's and unto God the things that are God's; and Paul, a prisoner, appeals unto Caesar.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jesus drew the line that every believer still walks: Caesar gets his coin, but God gets the heart. The emperor can stamp his image on money, but the image of God is stamped on us — and that is why my first loyalty is never to an empire.
